title: Partial-Year Use Standard — Measuring RideLink Value-Added Trip Use
content:
When a Non-Emergency Medical Transportation benefit had value-added trips for only part of a year, the year's use is measured so that a short year is compared fairly with a full one.

**Rule.** The year's use is measured against the months the benefit had trips that year, counted from the month the year's allotment load was posted through December: a benefit that had trips for six months or fewer has its debited trips annualized, multiplied by twelve and divided by those months; a benefit that had trips for seven to eleven months has one trip added to its debited trips for each month without trips; a benefit that had trips all twelve months has its use counted as debited.

The months with trips include both the month the load was posted and December.

## Month bands

| Month the year's allotment load was posted | Months with trips | Measured use |
|---|---|---|
| January | 12 | Debited trips as they stand |
| February to June | 11 to 7 | Debited trips plus one for each month without trips |
| July to December | 6 to 1 | Debited trips times twelve, divided by the months with trips |

## Worked figures

*Hypothetical years:*

- Load posted in August: August to December is 5 months. 4 trips debited give 4 times twelve divided by 5, that is 9.6.
- Load posted in July: 6 months. 3 trips debited give 3 times twelve divided by 6, that is 6.
- Load posted in April: 9 months, 3 months without trips. 5 trips debited give 5 plus 3, that is 8.
- Load posted in January: 12 months. 10 trips debited give a use of 10.

The annualized figure is not rounded.
